article_title: The Impact of Watching Subtitled Animated Cartoons on Incidental Vocabulary Learning of ELT Students
citation: Ali Karakaş and Arif Sariçoban. (2011). The Impact of Watching Subtitled Animated Cartoons on Incidental Vocabulary Learning of ELT Students. Teaching English with Technology, 12(4), 3-15. http://www.tewtjournal.org
title: Vocabulary Knowledge Scale (VKS), 5-point self-report instrument adapted with 18 target verbs
description: The study used Wesche and Paribakht's (1996) 5-point self-report Vocabulary Knowledge Scale, adapted with 18 infrequently used target verbs drawn from two Family Guy episodes. The scale "allows to specify the stages of vocabulary acquisition from first exposure to production" and shows students' partial knowledge; levels run from not remembering the word to using it in a sentence. Responses at levels 3-5 were checked for accuracy and downgraded one level if incorrect.
requirements: Responses claiming knowledge (levels 3-5) require researcher checking of the synonym, translation, or sentence produced, with incorrect responses downgraded one level
constraints: The article notes Meara's (1996) criticism that the scale's description of word knowledge is rather simple and does not account for more detailed knowledge developing over time; the authors state its goal was only to identify initial stages of vocabulary development
target_learning_goals: measuring stages of vocabulary knowledge development from recognition to production
examples: Pilot tests with similar freshman ELT students at Suleyman Demirel University yielded Cronbach's Alpha .864, after which six verbs were eliminated, leaving 18 target words
key_sources: Ali Karakaş and Arif Sariçoban. (2011). The Impact of Watching Subtitled Animated Cartoons on Incidental Vocabulary Learning of ELT Students. Teaching English with Technology, 12(4), 3-15. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1144953

article_title: The Power of Graphic Organizers: Effects on Students' Word-Learning and Achievement Emotions in Social Studies
citation: İlter, İ. (2016). The Power of Graphic Organizers: Effects on Students' Word-Learning and Achievement Emotions in Social Studies. Australian Journal of Teacher Education, 41(1). http://ro.ecu.edu.au/ajte/vol41/iss1/3
title: Vocabulary Knowledge Scale (VKS) format test adapted to Turkish for social studies vocabulary
description: The VKS is a self-report vocabulary measure developed by Wesche and Paribakht (1996) with four stages ranging from "Do not know the word" to being able to use the word in a sentence. The researcher adapted it to Turkish and administered it as pretest and posttest for 15 target social studies words such as public opinion, democracy and sovereignty. Scoring runs from 1 point for unknown words to 4 points for correct original-sentence usage.
requirements: Administered with an answer key of meanings, synonyms-antonyms and correct usage examples reviewed by Turkish Language experts for language validity
constraints: Adapted for fourth-grade social studies vocabulary in Turkish; validity checked with sixth- and seventh-grade English-knowing students (r= .83) and a factor analysis on N=300 fourth-graders
target_learning_goals: depth of vocabulary knowledge of social studies target words, including recognition and productive sentence usage
examples: Used as pretest and posttest in the 7-week quasi-experiment comparing graphic-organizer instruction with the C(2)QU contextual process
key_sources: İlter, İ. (2016). The Power of Graphic Organizers: Effects on Students' Word-Learning and Achievement Emotions in Social Studies. Australian Journal of Teacher Education, 41(1). http://ro.ecu.edu.au/ajte/vol41/iss1/3
